items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: maybe five or six months into my hanging out with them I learned like 30, 35 tunes all by ear, that I would play with his band

ctx.x: Okay so my thing is this. And I share this openly with my students and I let them know, don’t be scared. I am the poster child for dyslexia. So the whole idea of the note and how it matches up to a chord, that was a nightmare for me. I knew what the note sounded like, and I could hear the chords, but making the match of the mathematics was a very major challenge for me. So I could play on “Rhythm” changes, I could play “Rhythm” changes, I could do standards, because I had really good ears, before I figured out…

Baroque and Renaissance music. So I remember sitting there and there was this woman dressed up all beautifully and she’s playing the harpsichord, and I say, in my ignorant South Bronx fashion, I go, “Hey man, that’s bebop.” Because I could hear [scats] and I went, “Oh man that’s bebop.” You know. Because listen, when I was in high school my girlfriend at the time, her father was a jazz guitar player, Doc Russell. And he took an interest in my development and they would have jam sessions at the house and I would…
